fields.label: HTTP Content Routing
fields.help: Each content routing policy can either have its own web protection profile or inherit the web protection profile from this server policy.

fields.label: Match Once
fields.help: Evaluate the set of headers in the first request only. Following requests within the same single TCP connection will be forwarded to the same server pool.

fields.label: Protected Hostnames
fields.help:
A list of hostnames that FortiWeb should allow/block
in the HTTP "Host" header.
No Protected Hostnames Policy will Allow All.

fields.label: Client Real IP
fields.help: Enable to use the client source IP and port when connecting to the backend server. Configure FortiWeb as the default gateway on the backend server to ensure the reply goes through FortiWeb.

fields.label: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS
fields.help:
Redirect all HTTP requests to HTTPS.
Requests will not be blocked on HTTP-based requests,
but will be subjected to blocking once the redirected,
HTTPS request is received.

fields.label: Redirect Naked Domain
fields.help: Redirect naked domain requests to "www" domain requests.

fields.label: Traffic Mirror
fields.help: Enable to mirror all traffic to third party devices per the Traffic Mirror policy.

fields.label: Retry On
fields.help: Configure whether to retry a failed connection or HTTP request

fields.label: Monitor Mode
fields.help:
Requests which would normally be blocked
will be treated as "Alert Only".
Recommended for new deployments and testing.

fields.label: ZTNA Profile
fields.help: When ZTNA Profile is selected, HTTP Service, Redirect HTTP to HTTPS will be disabled, and Certificate Verification for HTTPS must be configured.

fields.label: Allow List
fields.help: Select to use Policy Based Allow list instead of Global Allow List

fields.label: One Click GSLB Server
fields.help: FortiGSLB Cloud needs about 1-3 minutes to process the GSLB configuration from Fortiweb, please confirm the configuration in FortiGSLB Cloud after about 3 minutes.

fields.label: Enable Server Name Indication(SNI)
fields.help: Server Name Indication allows multiple HTTPS websites to be served by the same IP address without requiring all those sites to use the same certificate.

fields.label: Enable URL Based Client Certificate
fields.help: Defines for which URLs the client will need to submit a certificate, not work for HTTP2.

fields.label: Enable SSL Ciphers Group
fields.help: Use SSL Ciphers Group

fields.label: SSL/TLS Encryption Level
fields.help: FortiWeb will allow only certain cipher suites depending on the encryption level defined.

fields.label: Disable Client-Initiated SSL Renegotiation
fields.help: Ignores client requests for SSL/TLS renegotiation to protect against DoS attacks that use the disproportionate server-side computing burden during SSL/TLS renegotiation.

fields.label: Client Certificate Forwarding
fields.help: FortiWeb will forward client certificate information to the web server via a specific HTTP header field.

fields.label: Add HSTS Header
fields.help: Add an HSTS header ("Strict-Transport-Security") to responses to declare that browsers should only interact with this web server using secure HTTPS connections.

fields.label: Add HPKP Header
fields.help: HTTP Public Key Pinning (HPKP) is a security mechanism delivered via an HTTP header that ensures clients that the web server certificate is authentic.

fields.label: Inherit Web Protection Profile
fields.help: If disabled, choose the web protection profile to be applied to this content routing policy.</br>If enabled, the web protection profile from the server policy will be automatically applied to this content routing policy.
